newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says PNG steel operations resuming.
newsitem.headline: BHP says PNG steel operations resuming.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Thursday it was restarting its steel processing operations in Papua New Guinea with the aim of returning to normal output by April 1.
"We expect our steel plants will resume normal operation after the Easter break," a BHP Steel spokeswoman told Reuters.

Last Sunday, BHP closed its Port Moresby steel processing centre and evacuated 10 to 15 staff and their families due to security concerns after a confrontation between the prime minister and sacked defence force commander plunged the nation into political crisis.
Staff at other BHP steel plants in PNG were told to come to work only if they wanted.
Wednesday's stepping aside of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan and his finance and defence ministers has since defused the crisis.
The BHP spokeswoman said there had been some arson damage at a roll-forming facility in Lae but output would not be affected.
She said most of the evacuated staff would return by April 1, adding some had decided to take holidays.
Earlier BHP Copper chief executive Jim Lewis said the company was committed to PNG as a place for future investment.
